posts.title: The Streaming Lakehouse, Part 5: Freshness per Plant Question
posts.description: Questions about a telemetry stream assume different freshness. This part places four invented monitoring and analytics questions against what each of the three designs documents about freshness: a commit trigger, compaction and publication rules, and a tiering interval.

posts.title: The Streaming Lakehouse, Part 4: Fluss: The Tier in Front of the Lake
posts.description: Apache Fluss keeps recent rows in its own tables and a tiering service commits them to the lake on a set interval. Union read, documented for Flink and Spark, queries both. What the v1.0.0 documentation says, and where it is silent.

posts.title: The Streaming Lakehouse, Part 3: Paimon's LSM Tables and Their Iceberg View
posts.description: In Apache Paimon each bucket of a primary-key table holds a log-structured merge tree. Frequent commits add sorted runs that compaction merges, and an Iceberg reader sees what compaction and publication have promoted.
